title: Functorial local ringed relocalization along a sheaf map
statement: Work with sites small in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $g:(\mathcal E,R)\to(\mathcal F,S)$ be a ringed-topos morphism [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], with $\mathcal E,\mathcal F$ categories of sheaves of sets. For a sheaf $A\in\mathcal E$, the slice $\mathcal E/A$ consists of arrows to $A$, with ring $R_A=(R\times A\to A)$; define $S_B$ similarly. Given $B\in\mathcal F$ and $s:A\to g^{-1}B$, there is a ringed-topos morphism $g_s:(\mathcal E/A,R_A)\to(\mathcal F/B,S_B)$ with inverse image $$(H\to B)\longmapsto(g^{-1}H\times_{g^{-1}B,s}A\to A).$$ Its structural map is the restriction of $g^\sharp:g^{-1}S\to R$, and its composites with the slice projections agree with $g$ followed by the source slice projection, up to the canonical ring-compatible isomorphism. A locally ringed topos here means a ringed topos whose ring sheaf has locally $a$ or $1-a$ invertible for every section $a$, and whose equalizer of $0,1$ is the initial sheaf. A local morphism means that its square of ring sheaves and unit subsheaves is cartesian. If $g$ is local between locally ringed topoi, both ringed slices are locally ringed and $g_s$ is local. If $a:A\prime\to A$, $b:B\prime\to B$, and $s\prime:A\prime\to g^{-1}B\prime$ satisfy $g^{-1}(b)s\prime=sa$, the square formed by $g_s,g_{s\prime}$ and the two slice restriction morphisms commutes up to the canonical ring-compatible isomorphism. These comparisons respect identities and successive restrictions. For a ring-compatible natural isomorphism $t:g^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}k^{-1}$ and $s_k=t_Bs$, the component maps $t_H$ and $\mathrm{id}_A$ induce a ring-compatible isomorphism $g_s\cong k_{s_k}$ on slices. These slice comparisons are natural on every sheaf and compatible with the structure-ring maps.

source.place: Tag 04J8 (lemma-relocalize-morphism-ringed-topoi), Tag 04IH (lemma-localize-morphism-locally-ringed-topoi), with sites.tex Tag 04IV (lemma-relocalize-morphism-topoi) and its fibre-product formula. The two-isomorphism comparison is the explicit fibre-product map also used in spaces-properties.tex Tag 04M6 (lemma-faithful).

proof.text: Write $L=g^{-1}$. The sheaf categories have finite limits by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise]. By [lem-sfb-left-exact-left-adjoint-slices], the arrowwise functor $L_B:\mathcal F/B\to\mathcal E/LB$, $(H\to B)\mapsto(LH\to LB)$, is left exact and has a right adjoint: the hypotheses hold because $L\dashv g_*$ and $L$ is left exact by [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. The slices are sheaf topoi on the small element sites supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction]. For this purely set-theoretic assertion one may apply that lemma with the terminal, one-element commutative ring sheaf, independently of the given $R,S$.

source.place: Tags 0791 (lemma-localize-topos-site) and 04H1 (lemma-localize-morphism-topoi); arrowwise left exact adjunction on slices.

proof.text: Regard $s:A\to LB$ as an object of $\mathcal E/LB$. Its localization is $\mathcal E/A$ by the iterated-slice clause of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction]; denote its left exact inverse image by $s^*$. It sends $Z\to LB$ to $Z\times_{LB}A\to A$: in the iterated slice, product with the object $s$ is precisely this fibre product. One can check the formula in the element-site equivalence by taking the fibre over each section of $A$. Thus $P_s=s^*L_B$ has right adjoint the composite of the two right adjoints and preserves finite limits. It defines a geometric morphism $g_s$ with exactly the asserted inverse-image formula. The same localization construction gives all slice projection and slice restriction morphisms used below.

source.place: Tags 04GZ (lemma-localize-topos), 04IR (lemma-relocalize-topos) and 04IV (lemma-relocalize-morphism-topoi), factorization and fibre-product formula.

proof.text: The element-site equivalence in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction], applied with the one-element ring, sends $R\times A\to A$ to $(U,a)\mapsto R(U)$: its fibre consists exactly of pairs $(r,a)$, and all ring operations act on $r$. This works for arbitrary ring sheaves, without a commutativity assumption. Finite-product preservation identifies $P_s(S_B)$ with $g^{-1}S\times A\to A$. Define $g_s^\sharp=g^\sharp\times1_A:g^{-1}S\times A\to R\times A$. It preserves the ring operations because $g^\sharp$ does, so [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] makes $g_s$ a ringed morphism. If $j_A,j_B$ denote the projections, the same product calculation gives $P_sj_B^{-1}H\cong j_A^{-1}g^{-1}H$ by $(x,a)\mapsto(x,a)$. On $H=S$ this identification carries the structural map to $g^\sharp\times1_A$; the projection structural maps are identities on the restricted rings. Hence $j_Bg_s\cong gj_A$ as ringed morphisms, naturally on every sheaf.

source.place: Tags 04IF (lemma-localize-morphism-ringed-topoi) and 04J8 (lemma-relocalize-morphism-ringed-topoi), restricted structural map and projection square.

proof.text: Suppose now that $R,S$ satisfy the two local-ring conditions in the statement. On the element site for $A$ supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction], the fibre calculation of step 3 identifies $R_A(U,a)$ with $R(U)$, with covers those of $U$. A cover on which $r$ or $1-r$ is a unit lifts to the cover $(U_i,a|_{U_i})$; its inverses are the same sections. Thus the first local-ring condition holds for $R_A$. The equalizer of $0,1$ in $R_A$ is $j_A^{-1}$ of the equalizer in $R$, since this inverse image preserves finite limits. It is initial, since a left adjoint preserves the initial object (its Hom set into any object is a singleton by adjunction). The identical argument for $S,B$ proves that both slices are locally ringed, including empty slices.

source.place: Tag 04IH (lemma-localize-morphism-locally-ringed-topoi), part (5) and final alternative direct proof; Tag 04H8 (definition-locally-ringed-topos).

proof.text: For any ring sheaf $T$, the subsheaf $T^\times$ is identified with the sheaf of pairs $(x,y)$ satisfying $xy=yx=1$, by first projection: a two-sided inverse is unique, since $y=y(xz)=(yx)z=z$. It is therefore specified by finite limits, so every left exact inverse image preserves this description of units. In particular $P_s(S_B^\times)\cong j_A^{-1}g^{-1}(S^\times)$ and $R_A^\times\cong j_A^{-1}(R^\times)$. Under these identifications and step 3, the unit square of $g_s^\sharp$ is $j_A^{-1}$ of the unit square of $g^\sharp$. When $g$ is local the latter is cartesian; finite-limit preservation of $j_A^{-1}$ makes the former cartesian. This proves locality, without any hypothesis on points or on a site functor inducing $g$.

source.place: Tag 04HA (definition-morphism-locally-ringed-topoi); Tag 04IH, parts (7)-(8), and proof of lemma-locally-ringed-intrinsic-morphism immediately preceding it.

proof.text:
Let $p:H\to B$ and $g^{-1}(b)s'=sa$. The inverse images along the two paths in the restriction square are naturally identified by
$$(g^{-1}H\times_{g^{-1}B}A)\times_AA'\ \cong\ g^{-1}(H\times_BB')\times_{g^{-1}B'}A'.$$
Explicitly both have coordinates $(x,a')$ with $g^{-1}(p)(x)=s(a(a'))$: on the right the extra $B'$ coordinate is forced to be $s'(a')$. Finite-limit preservation of $g^{-1}$ gives the displayed identification. These maps are natural in $H$, since a sheaf map acts on the $x$ coordinate, and are inverse by the fibre-product universal property. On $S_B$ they are the identity on the $g^{-1}S$ and $A'$ coordinates, so both structural maps are $g^\sharp\times1_{A'}$. This is the required ring-compatible square. For identities the comparison fixes both coordinates; for successive restrictions, either composite sends $(x,a'')$ to the same pair. Equality of the projections into each fibre product proves coherence, also with the projection comparisons of step 3.

source.place: Tag 04IV, final fibre-product identity in the proof; sites-modules.tex Tag 04J8, functoriality square.

proof.text:
Let $t:g^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}k^{-1}$ be ring-compatible, so $k^\sharp t_S=g^\sharp$, and put $s_k=t_Bs$. Naturality $k^{-1}(p)t_H=t_Bg^{-1}(p)$ gives a map of pullbacks
$$g^{-1}H\times_{g^{-1}B,s}A\longrightarrow k^{-1}H\times_{k^{-1}B,s_k}A,\qquad(x,a)\longmapsto(t_H(x),a).$$
Its inverse uses $t_H^{-1}$; naturality in $H$ follows from that of $t$. At the restricted structure ring this is $t_S\times1_A$, and ring compatibility is exactly $(k^\sharp\times1_A)(t_S\times1_A)=g^\sharp\times1_A$. It therefore gives the asserted ring-compatible isomorphism on slices. The maps of step 6 only retain or substitute the $A$ coordinate, while this map acts only on $x$; consequently their composites agree on both projections. This also gives compatibility under further restrictions, and identities or composites of $t$ act by the corresponding identities or composites on $x$.

source.place: Tag 04M6 (lemma-faithful), middle two-isomorphism on relocalized inverse images; explicit formula and ring compatibility.
